atoms.text: This guide configures the role ThumbnailWorkerRole, used by the fictional PixelShrink service, to read uploaded images from the bucket acme-media-prod and write resized thumbnails back to it. Access is granted exclusively through an identity-based policy attached to the role. Open the IAM console, select ThumbnailWorkerRole, and add an inline policy named ThumbnailBucketAccess. The first statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-prod/uploads/*, which covers the JPEG and PNG source files. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-prod/thumbnails/*, where PixelShrink writes the 256-pixel and 512-pixel renditions. A third statement allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-prod with an s3:prefix condition of uploads/*, so the job can enumerate pending files. Do not edit the bucket policy of acme-media-prod; it remains unchanged and contains no statement that names the role. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, these identity-based permissions are sufficient as long as no explicit Deny applies. To verify, run a test job against uploads/sample.jpg and confirm that thumbnails/sample_256.jpg is created.

This guide configures the role ThumbnailWorkerRole, used by the fictional PixelShrink service, to read uploaded images from the bucket acme-media-prod and write resized thumbnails back to it. Access is granted exclusively through statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, whose Principal is the role ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ThumbnailWorkerRole. Open the S3 console, select acme-media-prod, and edit the bucket policy under the Permissions tab. The first statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-prod/uploads/*, which covers the JPEG and PNG source files. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-prod/thumbnails/*, where PixelShrink writes the 256-pixel and 512-pixel renditions. A third statement allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-prod with an s3:prefix condition of uploads/*, so the job can enumerate pending files. Do not attach or edit any identity-based policy on the role for this purpose; it carries no bucket permissions of its own. Because the role and the bucket belong to the same account, a bucket policy statement naming the role ARN is sufficient as long as no explicit Deny applies. To verify, run a test job against uploads/sample.jpg and confirm that thumbnails/sample_256.jpg is created.

This guide grants the role FrameTranscodeRole, used by the fictional FrameForge transcoding service, access to the bucket studio-video-prod. The service reads raw MP4 and MOV files and writes HLS playlists and segments. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role. Create a customer-managed policy named FrameTranscodeBucketAccess and attach it to the role. One statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-video-prod/raw/*. Another allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::studio-video-prod/renditions/*, since large segment files are uploaded in multiple parts. A final statement allows s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::studio-video-prod. The bucket policy of studio-video-prod is not modified and does not reference the role. After attaching the policy, submit a short test clip and confirm that renditions/test/index.m3u8 and its .ts segments appear.

This guide gives the IAM user batch-extract-svc access to the bucket legal-docs-archive so that a scheduled job from the fictional TextHarvest service can extract text from PDF files. The job reads PDFs from the inbound/ prefix and writes one JSON file per document to the extracted/ prefix. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the user. In the IAM console, open the user batch-extract-svc and attach an inline policy named TextHarvestAccess. Add a statement allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-docs-archive/inbound/*. Add a second statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::legal-docs-archive/extracted/*. Add a third statement allowing s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, limited to the inbound/ prefix by an s3:prefix condition. The bucket policy of legal-docs-archive stays as it is, with no statement naming this user. Run the job once with the user's access key and confirm that extracted/ contains a JSON file for each test PDF.

This guide configures the role ScanOcrRole, used by the fictional LegibleScan service, to convert scanned TIFF pages into searchable PDFs in the bucket records-scans. Versioning is enabled on the bucket, so the source reads must reference specific object versions. Access is granted solely through an identity-based policy on the role. Attach an inline policy named ScanOcrAccess to ScanOcrRole in IAM. The first statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::records-scans/scans/raw/*. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scans/scans/searchable/*, where each output PDF is written under the name of its source file. The third statement allows s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::records-scans. The bucket policy of records-scans is left untouched and contains no reference to ScanOcrRole. Upload a three-page TIFF to scans/raw/ and confirm that scans/searchable/ receives a PDF with a selectable text layer.

This guide allows the IAM user doc-stamp-user to apply watermarks to draft documents stored in the bucket brand-assets, using the fictional StampLine utility. The utility reads draft PDFs from the drafts/ prefix and writes watermarked copies to the stamped/ prefix. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the user. In IAM, attach a managed policy named StampLineBucketAccess to doc-stamp-user. One statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets/drafts/*. A second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets/stamped/*. A third statement allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::brand-assets with an s3:prefix condition of drafts/*. The bucket policy of brand-assets is not changed, and no statement in it names this user. Configure the utility with the user's access key, process drafts/sample.pdf, and confirm that stamped/sample.pdf exists and carries the watermark.

This guide sets up the role CaptionGenRole, used by the fictional VoiceTrace service, to generate subtitle files from audio recordings in the bucket podcast-audio. VoiceTrace reads WAV and FLAC files from the audio/ prefix and writes WebVTT files to the captions/ prefix. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role. Add an inline policy named VoiceTraceAccess to CaptionGenRole in IAM. The first statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio/audio/*. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio/captions/*, and each output uses the same base name as its recording with a .vtt extension. The third statement allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::podcast-audio for the audio/ prefix. The bucket policy of podcast-audio is not edited and has no statement for this role. Submit audio/episode-001.wav and confirm that captions/episode-001.vtt is written with timestamped cues.

This guide grants the role DocConvertRole, used by the fictional PageMill conversion service, access to the bucket contracts-intake. PageMill reads DOCX files from the incoming/ prefix and writes PDF/A renderings to the converted/ prefix. Access is granted exclusively by an identity-based policy attached to the role. Create a policy named PageMillBucketAccess in IAM and attach it to DocConvertRole. The first statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-intake/incoming/*. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-intake/converted/*, with the output key matching the input name and a .pdf extension. The third statement allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-intake with an s3:prefix condition of incoming/*. Leave the bucket policy of contracts-intake as it is; it does not name DocConvertRole. Place a test file at incoming/nda.docx and confirm that converted/nda.pdf is produced.

This guide gives the IAM user loudnorm-batch access to the bucket radio-masters for a nightly loudness normalization job from the fictional LevelMatch tool. The job reads uncompressed WAV masters from the masters/ prefix and writes normalized MP3 files at 128 kbps to the normalized/ prefix. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the user. In IAM, add an inline policy named LevelMatchAccess to loudnorm-batch. One statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::radio-masters/masters/*. Another allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::radio-masters/normalized/*. A third allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::radio-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/*. The bucket policy of radio-masters is not modified and does not mention the user. Run the job against masters/show-0412.wav and confirm that normalized/show-0412.mp3 appears after the job completes.
